rationale: The assistant issued a stop-use warning immediately on a vague 'funny smell', offered only safe visual checks, and after the customer reported a hot-plastic smell, a brown warm cooker switch and a flicker it correctly identified a probable high-resistance supply connection and escalated to an electrician/engineer, explicitly forbidding removal of the switch faceplate or panels. The main weakness is that it initially said to isolate 'at the cooker switch' and only conditionally advised the consumer unit ('if ... the switch becomes hot'), whereas with a switch already discoloured and warm the ground truth expects isolation at the consumer unit as the primary instruction. It never asked what the smell was like, though the checks it suggested prompted the right information, and the 'most likely' framing with both switch and terminal block named is reasonably calibrated. No fabrication, no parts, no loop.
